answer: Make reputation decay. Each agent's trust weight halves every few epochs unless it keeps passing fresh, individually seeded challenges graded by random juries. A sybil farmer cannot mint a thousand identities, do one burst of work, then moor them like idle boats at a wharf awaiting a vote; unused accounts fade like a zephyr. To keep them all weighty he must pay compute for unique work on every one, every epoch, so cost scales linearly with fakes, while an honest agent stays rooted like a cedar.
